paragraphs: Meacharin tepillat arbit kede lehosip mechol al haqqodesh; vetzarik lehosip zeman shehu vadday layla. upoh irenu bagdad y" nohagim lehamtin ad sheyyaabor shelish shaa miqqeriat ha"muggerab"; vaateret rashe adoni abi zlh"h haya machmir lehamtin chatzi shaa, veal kol panim en rashshay lepachot min shelish shaa, shehu esrim daqqim achar qeriat ha"mogerab", kevan shennahagu bekak. vekatab harab "birke-yosep" za"l, shemmatza biktibat yad meharab chayyim veyittol za"l beshem rabbenu hay gaon za"l - tob sheyyihyeh haadam moshek umaarik baaniyyat "baruk Adonai hamborak leolam vaed" beippuqe shabbeta, veyoil lehatzlacha.

clarification.explanation: The evening prayer at the conclusion of the Sabbath is delayed in order to add from the profane onto the holy, and one must wait until it is certainly night. In Baghdad the custom was to wait until a third of an hour had passed, that is, twenty minutes, from the Muslim call to Maghrib (the time of sunset). The father of the Ben Ish Chai was stringent and waited half an hour, but in any case one should not wait less than a third of an hour, since this is the accepted custom. The Berachi Yosef wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Hai Gaon that it is good to draw out the answering of "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed forever and ever" at the conclusion of the Sabbath, and this is beneficial for success.
takeaways: The evening prayer at the conclusion of the Sabbath is delayed until it is certainly night, to add from the profane onto the holy
In Baghdad they waited a third of an hour, twenty minutes, and not less
It is good to draw out answering "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed forever and ever," which is beneficial for success

paragraphs: Leharamba"m za"l, mitzvat aseh min hattora leqaddesh hashshabbat bidbarim bitziato, velishar poseqim hu middibre soperim. velaken tiqqenu anshe keneset haggedola nosach "atta chonantanu" leamero bitpilla, ubazeh meqayyem haadam mitzvat leqaddesh hashshabbat bidbarim; veaach"k chazeru vetiqqenu chaza"l leqaddesho al hakkos, vetiqqenu nosach birkat hahabdala al hakkos millebad amirat "atta chonantanu" asher omerim bitpilla. vetzarik lehishtaddel lehabdil al hakkos velachazor acharayv, kederek shemmachazirin al mitzvot shehem chobat haggup, "p sheamar "atta chonantanu"; veraq im i epshar lo limtzo kos lehabdil alayv, az yotze yede chobato b"atta chonantanu" shebbattepilla. vachaza"l qabeu hahabdala bebirkat "atta chonen", mippene sheyyesh lah dimyon immah. veim shakach velo amar "atta chonantanu" beemtza habberaka hazzo shel "atta chonen": im amar "baruk atta Adonai" venizkar, ap-al-pi shello amar adayin "chonen haddaat", hare zeh mashlim habberaka lomar "chonen haddaat", veen tzarik lomar "atta chonantanu", shehare achar tepilla yabdil al hakkos, velaken gam b"shomea tepilla" lo yomar otah, veraq yizzaher shello laasot shum melaka achar tepilla qodem sheyyabdil al hakkos; abal im lo hizkir hashshem, ella kesheamar "baruk atta" nizkar, hare zeh yomar miyyad "atta chonantanu veku'" al hasseder, veyachtom "baruk et Adonai, chonen haddaat".

clarification.explanation: According to the Rambam there is a positive Torah commandment to sanctify the Sabbath with words also at its departure, while according to the other authorities this is a rabbinic commandment. Therefore the men of the Great Assembly instituted saying "Atah chonantanu" in the evening prayer, through which a person fulfills the commandment of distinguishing the Sabbath with words. Afterward the Sages instituted distinguishing also over a cup in the blessing of Havdalah, in addition to saying "Atah chonantanu" in the prayer. One should make an effort to perform Havdalah over a cup and seek out a cup as one seeks out a commandment that is a personal obligation, even though he has already said "Atah chonantanu." Only if no cup can be found does he fulfill his obligation with "Atah chonantanu" in the prayer. The Sages placed the Havdalah within the blessing of "Atah chonen" because of the similarity between them. If one forgot and did not say "Atah chonantanu" in its place: if he already said "Blessed are You, O Lord" at the end of the blessing and then remembers, he completes "Chonen hada'at" and does not go back, since he will perform Havdalah later over a cup in any case; therefore he should also not say it in "Shome'a tefillah," and should only be careful not to do work until he performs Havdalah over the cup. But if he had not yet mentioned God's name and remembers after "Blessed are You," he should immediately say "Atah chonantanu" in order and conclude with "Chonen hada'at."
takeaways: The commandment of Havdalah in words is fulfilled by saying "Atah chonantanu" in the prayer
The primary obligation is to perform Havdalah over a cup, which one should seek out as a personal obligation
Forgot and already said "Blessed are You, O Lord" — completes "Chonen hada'at" and does not go back, then performs Havdalah over the cup
Remembered before mentioning God's name — says "Atah chonantanu" in order

paragraphs: Ha deamarnu: im taa velo hizkir "atta chonantanu", deen tzarik leamerah b"shomea tepilla", haynu davqa im hu yodea sheyyesh lo kos lehabdil alayv, abal im yodea sheen lo kos lehabdil alayv, vegam lemachar lo yihyeh lo, hare zeh omer "atta chonantanu" b"shomea tepilla", kevan sheshshakach leamerah bebirkat "atta chonen", kedin mi sheshshakach sheela bebirkat hashshanim, sheomerah b"shomea tepilla". veim gam b"shomea tepilla" shakach velo amarah, tzarik lachazor ulehitpallel kede lomar "atta chonantanu", mippene shehu en lo kos lehabdil alayv, vegam yodea sheggam lemachar en lo kos. veim era lo ken betisha beab sheshshakach lomar "atta chonantanu" b"atta chonen", vegam lo amaro b"shomea tepilla", en tzarik lachazor ulehitpallel kede lomar "atta chonantanu", ap-al-pi shebballayla eno mabdil al hakkos, meachar sheyyodea hu sheyyabdil al hakkos bemotzae tisha beab; veraq yizzaher lomar belel tisha beab qodem asiyyat melaka birkat "hammabdil ben qodesh lechol" belo shem umalkut.

clarification.explanation: What we said, that one who forgot "Atah chonantanu" need not say it in "Shome'a tefillah," applies specifically when he knows he has a cup to perform Havdalah over. But if he knows he has no cup to perform Havdalah over, and will not have one tomorrow either, he should say "Atah chonantanu" in "Shome'a tefillah," like the law of one who forgot to ask for rain in the blessing of the years, which is said in "Shome'a tefillah." If he forgot it there too, he must pray again in order to say "Atah chonantanu," since he has no cup at all. But if this happened on the Ninth of Av, where he forgot "Atah chonantanu" both in its blessing and in "Shome'a tefillah," he need not pray again, even though at night he does not perform Havdalah over a cup, since he knows he will perform Havdalah over a cup at the conclusion of the Ninth of Av. He need only be careful to say, on the night of the Ninth of Av, before doing any work, "Blessed is He who distinguishes between the holy and the profane," without God's name and sovereignty.
takeaways: Forgot "Atah chonantanu" and has no cup today or tomorrow — says it in "Shome'a tefillah"
Forgot it there too and has no cup at all — must pray again
On the Ninth of Av he does not pray again, since he will perform Havdalah over a cup at the conclusion of the fast
On the night of the Ninth of Av, before work, he says "Blessed is He who distinguishes between the holy and the profane," without God's name and sovereignty

paragraphs: Katub bazzohar haqqadosh, parashat bereshit, dap yd: ubesheruta, mabdeli bitzlota, umabdeli al kos, pirche mittamman veku', yeuyyan sham. vekatabti sham, besiyyata dishmayya, behaggahotay al hazzohar, hakkavvana – shemmegareshim leotam mazziqim behadragot: utechilla omerim habdala bitzlota delachash, ubazeh neeqar venitlash koach happenimi shel hammazziqin; veachar-kak "shir shel pegaim", ubazeh neeqar venitlash koach haemtza shellahem; veachar-kak habdala beqol ram, ubazeh neeqar venitlash koach hachitzon shellahem, veaz pirche legamre veazeli lehu lemiddebara veku'; yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: The holy Zohar explains that at the conclusion of the Sabbath one performs Havdalah in the prayer and Havdalah over the cup, and through this the harmful spirits are driven away. The Ben Ish Chai explains that this expulsion happens in stages: first the Havdalah is said in the silent Amidah, which uproots the inner power of the harmful spirits. Then the "Song of Afflictions" is said, which uproots their intermediate power. Then Havdalah is performed over the cup aloud, which uproots their outer power, and then they fly off and depart completely into the wilderness. This is a halachah according to the esoteric tradition explaining the virtue of the order of the Havdalot at the conclusion of the Sabbath.
takeaways: The Havdalot at the conclusion of the Sabbath drive away the harmful spirits in stages
The silent Havdalah uproots their inner power, the "Song of Afflictions" the intermediate power, and the Havdalah aloud the outer power

paragraphs: Bemaqom sherubbam amme-haaretz veen yodeim lomar "atta chonantanu" al-peh, metzuvveh al shelicha-tzibbur lomar "atta chonantanu" kullo beqol ram, kede sheyyomru immo o yekavvenu laamirato. veayyen "kap-hachayyim", siman lt, ot t, yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: In a place where most of the congregation are unlearned and do not know how to say "Atah chonantanu" by heart, it is a commandment upon the prayer leader to say the entire "Atah chonantanu" aloud, so that they can say it with him or intend his saying of it and thereby fulfill the obligation of Havdalah in the prayer.
takeaways: In a place where most are unlearned, the prayer leader says "Atah chonantanu" aloud
The worshippers say it with him or intend his saying of it

paragraphs: Omerim "vayhi noam" achar tepillat haamida shel arbit, venohagim likpol pasuq "orek yamim assebeehu" lehashlim hamminyan. veal-pi hassod, inyan "vayhi noam" sheomerim bekol motzae-shabbat, hu inyan nipla vegadol meod, ki hu kede lehamshik tosepet qedushshat shabbat lekol yeme hashshabua habbaa ad shabbat haacheret, veal-ken, mizmor zeh shel "vayhi noam" tzarik leamero kullo meummad, ulepachot tomar pasuq zeh shel "vayhi noam" meummad veachar-kak tesheb. vehattaam hu: ki hakkavvana atta, kede leqabbel or hachozer min habbina hanniqra noam Adonai missod tosepet shabbat, velaken tzarik sheyyihyeh meummad; veatta tzarik haadam lehakin atzmo leqabbel or tosepet hashshabbat besheshet yeme hachol, ubeken yihyeh mikkelal : "vehitqaddishtem, vihyitem qadashim", shetztzarik haadam lehitqaddesh bime hachol miqqedushshat hashshabbat. veda, ki shene mine tosepet qedushshat shabbat nittosap beyom hashshabbat, vehem: haechad, al-yede kavvanat hattepillot shel shabbat, vehashsheni, al-yede kavvanat hasseudot; ukeneged hamshakat tosepet qedushshat shabbat lime hachol mibbechinat hasseudot, anachnu osin seuda rebiit bemotzae-shabbat, vekavvanatah hi, lehamshik or qedushshat seudot shabbat lekol seudot yeme hachol; ukeneged hamshakat tosepet qedushshat shabbat mibbechinat hattepillot, anachnu omerim mizmor zeh shel "vayhi noam", sheal-yede zeh anachnu mamshikim oto noam lekol tepillot hashshabua. velaken tob shekkol adam yomar bepiv qodem amirat "vayhi noam": hareni mekin atzmi leqabbel or tosepet qedushshat hashshabbat lime hachol, veetqaddesh beezrat hashshem bime hachol miqqedushshat hashshabbat kemo shetztzivvanu Adonai eloqenu betorato haqqedosha: "vehitqaddishtem, vihyitem qadashim". vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai eloqenu vealloqe abotenu, sheyyaaleh lepaneka keillu kavvanati bekol hakkavvanot hareuyot lekavven bazeh. veda, deap-al-pi shekkatebu happoseqim happashtanim deen lomar "vayhi noam" keshechal yom-tob beemtza hashshabua, mikkol maqom, al pi hassod tzarik leamero bekol motzae-shabbat, ukemo shekkatab harab chida" za"l b"birke-yosep", siman rtzh, veken katab b"shalme-tzibbur", dap rch, ammud g. ubeseper "chesed lealpayim" katab: al pi hassod rauy lomar "vayhi noam" apillu bemotzae-shabbat shechal bechol-hammoed, veken rauy laasot behetznea leket. vehinneh poh irenu bagdad y", haya hamminhag miqqadmat dena shello lomar "vayhi noam" keshechal yom-tob beemtza hashshabua; utehillot lael, qodem kamma shanim tiqqanti besiyyata dishmayya hamminhag bekol batte-kenesiyyot asher poh irenu bagdad, lomar "vayhi noam" ad sop hammizmor bekol motzae-shabbat been hepresh kelal.

clarification.explanation: "Vayehi no'am" is said after the Amidah of the evening prayer at the conclusion of the Sabbath, and it is customary to repeat the verse "length of days will I satisfy him" to complete the count. According to the esoteric tradition, saying "Vayehi no'am" every conclusion of the Sabbath has a very lofty significance, since it is meant to draw an addition from the holiness of the Sabbath into all the days of the coming week. Therefore the entire psalm should be said standing, or at least the verse "Vayehi no'am" itself should be said standing, and only afterward should one sit, in order to receive the light of the addition of the Sabbath. Two kinds of additional holiness are added on the Sabbath: one through the intention of the prayers, and one through the intention of the meals. Corresponding to drawing the addition from the aspect of the meals, a fourth meal is held at the conclusion of the Sabbath; and corresponding to drawing it from the aspect of the prayers, "Vayehi no'am" is said. It is good to say, before "Vayehi no'am": "Behold I am preparing myself to receive the light of the addition of the holiness of the Sabbath for the weekdays, and I shall be sanctified during the weekdays from the holiness of the Sabbath; and may it be Your will that it rise before You as if I had intended all the proper intentions to be intended in this." Although the plain-sense halachic authorities wrote that "Vayehi no'am" is not said when a festival falls in the middle of the week, according to the esoteric tradition it is said at every conclusion of the Sabbath, and the Ben Ish Chai instituted in all the synagogues of Baghdad that it be said to the end of the psalm without exception.
takeaways: "Vayehi no'am" is said at the conclusion of the Sabbath, repeating "length of days will I satisfy him"
According to the esoteric tradition it draws an addition of the Sabbath's holiness into the weekdays; the psalm, or at least "Vayehi no'am" itself, is said standing
Corresponding to the addition of the meals, a fourth meal is held; corresponding to the prayers, "Vayehi no'am" is said
According to the esoteric tradition, "Vayehi no'am" is said at every conclusion of the Sabbath, even when a festival falls in the middle of the week

paragraphs: Inyan qedushshat "uba letziyyon" sheomerim belel motzae-shabbat, hakkavvana hi lehamshik hearat olam haatzilut asher besod tosepet shabbat el olam habberia, ki sham bechinat qedushshat "uba letziyyon goel", vekavvanatenu hi lehamshik tosepet haqqedushsha hahi bibria, kede shettitqayyem kol sheshet yeme hachol ad shabbat haacheret, velaken en qedushsha zo neemeret belayla acheret zulat motzae-shabbat, mippene deen beyadenu koach lehamshik hearat haatzilut bibria ella ballayla hazzot velo bishar lelot hachol, ukemo shekkatab bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar-hakkavvanot, velaken tzarik lehizzaher bah meod.

clarification.explanation: The Kedushah of "Uva LeTzion" said on the night at the conclusion of the Sabbath serves, according to the esoteric tradition, to draw the illumination of the World of Atzilut — in the secret of the addition of the Sabbath — into the World of Creation (Beriah), so that this holiness endure throughout all six weekdays until the following Sabbath. For this reason this Kedushah is not said on any other night besides the conclusion of the Sabbath, since only on this night do we have the power to draw the illumination of Atzilut into Beriah, and not on the other weeknights, as is explained in the words of the Ari in Sha'ar HaKavanot. Therefore one must be very careful with it.
takeaways: The Kedushah of "Uva LeTzion" at the conclusion of the Sabbath draws the illumination of Atzilut into Beriah for all the weekdays
This Kedushah is not said on any other night, since only at the conclusion of the Sabbath is there power to draw it
One must be very careful with it

paragraphs: Tzarik lehizzaher bekos hahabdala bekol haddebarim shekkatabnu al kos shel qiddush. vekatab harab chayyim veyittol za"l beshaar-hakkavvanot: tob shello lehattil mayim bekos shel habdala beshum open; yeuyyan sham. venireh li, mah shekkatab "beshum open", kavvanato lomar – ben im yannicha hammayim bakkos qodem sheyyannicha hayyayin, ben im yannicha hammayim achar hayyayin kishar mezigot, uben im yeareb hammayim betok hatztzelochit veachar-kak yitten hayyayin bakkos.

clarification.explanation: One must be careful about the cup of Havdalah in all the same respects said regarding the cup of Kiddush, such as that it be whole, clean, and full. The Ari wrote in Sha'ar HaKavanot that it is good not to add any water at all to the cup of Havdalah, in any manner whatsoever. The Ben Ish Chai explains that "in any manner whatsoever" means whether one puts the water in the cup before the wine, or after the wine as in mixing, or first mixes the water in a small vessel and then pours the wine into the cup.
takeaways: The laws of the cup of Havdalah are like those of the cup of Kiddush
It is good not to add any water at all to the cup of Havdalah
The prohibition applies in every manner: water before the wine, after it, or premixed in a small vessel

paragraphs: Beinyan atze besamim, meporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar-hakkavvanot: meotam shette aguddot hadas sheyyesh leka min shabbat shehem meshullashim, tiqqach mehem atta belel motzae-shabbat shelosha hadassim kesherim, vetaricha bahem beet birkat "atze besamim"; vetzarik sheyyihyu shelosha hadassim ellu qeshurim qesher echad vaagudda achat; vetikkavvan lehashir leka koach mittosepet nepesh rucha uneshama shennittosepu leka beshabbat, vezeh naaseh leka atta al-yede shelosha hadassim ellu beherichaka mehem. ukebar noda dekol peullot lel motzae-shabbat hem kede lehashir cheleq mittosepet qedushshat shabbat lime hachol habbaim, vekannizkar kol zeh beshaar-hakkavvanot. vekatab beseper "keter-malkut": kesheyyaricha – yimshok veyishab harecha bechatemo shelosha hamshakot usheibot bezo achar zo keneged nepesh rucha uneshama, vegam atta yekavven bemachshabto bearba tebot ellu shehem: "recha nichocha ishsha lah'".

clarification.explanation: Regarding the blessing "Who creates fragrant trees" at the conclusion of the Sabbath, the Ari wrote that from the two bundles of three myrtle branches a person had on the Sabbath, he should take three valid myrtle branches at the conclusion of the Sabbath and smell them at the time of the blessing, and they should be bound together in a single bundle. He should intend to retain within himself the power of the additional nefesh, ruach, and neshamah that were added to him on the Sabbath, since all the actions of the conclusion of the Sabbath are meant to retain a portion of the addition of the Sabbath's holiness for the weekdays. It is written in the book Keter Malchut that when smelling, one should draw the scent into the nose in three separate inhalations, corresponding to nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, and intend in his mind the four words "a sweet savor, an offering by fire to the Lord."
takeaways: A blessing is recited over three valid myrtle branches bound together
One intends to retain the power of the additional nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of the Sabbath
One draws the scent in three inhalations corresponding to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, intending "a sweet savor, an offering by fire to the Lord"

paragraphs: Yizzaher sheyyittol hahadas bishat beraka veyaricha bo kederek gedilato; vetzarik sheyyochazehu beyamin, ukeshehu beatzmo mebarek al hakkos deaz ochez hahadas bismolo, tzarik shebbishat beraka shel hahadas yochaz hakkos bismolo vehahadas bimino, veachar sheyyebarek "meore haesh" yachazor hakkos limino vibarek alayv birkat hahabdala, ki kol dabar shemmebarek alayv rauy leechoz beyamin; veachar shemmebarek al hahadas lo yizreqennu baaretz, ella yasim oto becheqo, o yimserennu leechad mibbene beto. vekatub beseper "tora lishmah": hahadas shel shabbat, lo yizreqennu achar motzae-shabbat sheyyihyeh im hazzebel laashpa, ella yatzniennu ad sheyyityabbesh, veyannichennu behassaqat hattannur shel lachmi shabbat.

clarification.explanation: One should be careful to hold the myrtle at the time of the blessing and smell it in the direction of its growth, with the leaves pointing upward. The myrtle should be held in the right hand. If one is himself reciting the blessing over the cup, holding the cup in his left hand, then at the time of the blessing over the myrtle he should hold the cup in his left hand and the myrtle in his right; after the blessing of "Who creates the lights of fire" he should return the cup to the right hand and recite the Havdalah over it, since anything one blesses should properly be held in the right hand. After blessing over the myrtle, one should not throw it on the ground, but place it in his lap or hand it to a member of his household. It is written in the book Torah LiShmah that the myrtle used on the Sabbath should not be thrown into the garbage with the trash, but should be set aside until it dries and then placed in the fire used to bake the Sabbath bread.
takeaways: The myrtle is held in the right hand and smelled in the direction of its growth
One who is himself reciting the blessing over the cup holds the myrtle in the right hand and the cup in the left during its blessing, then switches for Havdalah
The myrtle should not be thrown on the ground, but placed in one's lap or given to a household member
The Sabbath myrtle should not be thrown in the trash, but set aside to dry for use in baking the Sabbath bread

paragraphs: Im en lo hadas, yebarek shel shear mine besamim sheyyesh bahem recha tob. vetakshit shel zehubim shettolin hannashim betzavvaran al haddaddim umannichim bo besamim sheqqorin "qernpil", asur lebarek alayv, dezeh niqra besamim shel erva, veim berak alayv bemotzae-shabbat, lo yatza yede chobato, vetzarik lachazor ulebarek al besamim kesherim.

clarification.explanation: If one has no myrtle, he should recite the blessing over other fragrant spices that have a good smell. A gold ornament that women hang around their necks containing a perfume called "karanful" (clove) — one may not recite the blessing over it, since this is considered a perfume associated with intimacy (ervah). If one recited the blessing over it at the conclusion of the Sabbath, he has not fulfilled his obligation, and must recite the blessing again over valid spices.
takeaways: No myrtle — the blessing is recited over other fragrant spices
A perfume in a women's neck ornament is considered a perfume of intimacy, and the blessing may not be recited over it
If it was blessed over, the obligation was not fulfilled, and the blessing must be repeated over valid spices

paragraphs: Tiqqenu chaza"l lebarek "bore meore haesh" bemotzae-shabbat, zakar lemah shennatan haqqadosh-baruk-hu dea beadam harishon lechaddesh yetziat haur bemotzae shabbat – shellaqach shette abanim vehiqqishan zo bazo veyatza mehen ur (pesachim nd.); velaken yakol lebarek al haur shehotzio yisrael atta bemotzae-shabbat meabanim vekayyotze, chutz mimmotzae yom hakkippurim deen mebarekim al zeh, ella raq al or sheshshabat, dehatam yesh taam acher libraka zo. vaashashit shehidliqa meereb shabbat venishara deloqeh bemotzae shabbat, mebarek aleha; abal ner shehudlaq bashshabbat atzmo - kevan dehudlaq beissur - en mebarekim alayv bemotzae shabbat, vaapillu hidliqo nakeri letzorek atzmo, en mebarekim alayv, mippene sheim haya yisrael madliqo haya ober alayv, vahare zeh dino kener shehidliqu yisrael. veim berak al ner zeh shehidliqu yisrael o hannakeri beshabbat, tzarik lachazor ulebarek al or acher; mihu, im hidliq yisrael o hannakeri et hanner beshabbat letzorek choleh sheyyesh bo sakkana o letzorek chayya shehayu tzerikim lanner, en zo meleket abera, umebarekim al ner zeh bemotza"sh.

clarification.explanation: The Sages instituted reciting "Who creates the lights of fire" at the conclusion of the Sabbath, in remembrance of the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Adam the wisdom to discover the emergence of fire at the conclusion of the Sabbath, when he struck two stones together and fire came out of them. Therefore the blessing is recited over light that Israel now produces at the conclusion of the Sabbath from stones, except at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, when the blessing is recited only over light that "rested," that is, that was already burning before the fast. A lamp lit before the Sabbath and left burning at the conclusion of the Sabbath is blessed over. But a candle lit on the Sabbath itself in violation of the law is not blessed over, and even if a non-Jew lit it for his own purposes, it is not blessed over, since had a Jew lit it, it would have been a transgression. If one recited the blessing over such a candle, he must recite the blessing again over another light. But if a Jew or a non-Jew lit the candle on the Sabbath for the sake of a dangerously ill patient, or for the sake of a woman in labor, for whom a candle was needed, this is not a forbidden act of labor, and the blessing is recited over it at the conclusion of the Sabbath.
takeaways: "Who creates the lights of fire" is said in remembrance of Adam's discovery of fire
At the conclusion of Yom Kippur, the blessing is over light that rested from before the fast
A lamp lit before the Sabbath is blessed over; a candle lit on the Sabbath in violation of the law is not
A candle lit on the Sabbath for a dangerously ill patient or a woman in labor is blessed over

paragraphs: Nakeri shehidliq bemotza"sh et hanner minner shel yisrael, mebarekim alayv; abal im hannakeri hidliq et hanner minner shel nakeri, en mebarekim alayv, gezera shemma yabou lebarek al ner shehidliq hannakeri beshabbat; ubediabad, im abar uberak al ner zeh, en tzarik lachazor ulebarek. veim hannakeri hotzi or bemotza"sh meabanim vekayyotze, vehidliq hannakeri et hanner mizzeh haesh shehotzio hannakeri, yesh omerim demuttar lebarek alayv, veyesh oserim; ulekattechilla yesh lachush ledibre haoserim, velo yebarek ella ad sheyyadliq hayisrael ner acher mizzeh, vibarek al hanner sheyyadliq hayisrael. vekol halakot ellu hem metzuyim harbeh etzel baale battim sheyyesh lahem shepachot umesharetim nakerim bebetam. veda od deen mebarekim al ner shemmadliqim likbod bet-hakkeneset o limnuchat hammetim.

clarification.explanation: A non-Jew who, at the conclusion of the Sabbath, lit a candle from a Jew's candle — the blessing is recited over it. But if the non-Jew lit a candle from another non-Jew's candle, the blessing is not recited over it, as a decree lest people come to bless over a candle a non-Jew lit on the Sabbath itself. After the fact, if one recited the blessing over such a candle, he need not recite it again. If the non-Jew produced fire at the conclusion of the Sabbath from stones and lit a candle from it, some say it is permitted to bless over it and some forbid it; as the primary practice one should follow the stringent opinion and not recite the blessing until a Jew lights another candle from it and the blessing is recited over the Jew's candle. These laws are relevant for householders who have non-Jewish servants. Furthermore, the blessing is not recited over a candle lit in honor of the synagogue or in honor of the dead, since it was not made for light but for honor.
takeaways: A non-Jew who lit from a Jew's candle — the blessing is recited over it
A non-Jew who lit from another non-Jew's candle — as the primary practice, not blessed over, though after the fact one need not repeat the blessing
A non-Jew who produced fire from stones — as the primary practice, a Jew should light from it and the blessing be recited over the Jew's candle
The blessing is not recited over a candle lit in honor of the synagogue or of the dead

paragraphs: Haya hanner betok hakkeli sheqqorin "pnr" (panas rechob), vaapillu betok keli zekukit, en mebarekim alayv ad sheyyireh gup hashshalhebet mammash beli hepseq; velaken apillu im hanner galuy umopia or harbeh bekol maqom, veraq yesh bene-adam omedim betziddo veeno roeh et shalhebet hanner, eno mebarek. veap al pi sheroeh et shalhebet hanner, tzarik sheyyitqareb leoro bikde sheyyukal lehakkir ben matbea medina zo lematbea medina acheret shemmiddatam ukemotam shava. vesuma lo yebarek. vekatub beseper "tora lishmah": ap al pi demin haddin, kol sheyyukal lehabchin ben matbea lematbea rashshay lebarek, mikkol maqom metzuvveh min hammubchar sheyyitqareb el hanner beyoter, sheyyaggia lo haur beshopea merubbeh.

clarification.explanation: If the candle is inside a lantern, even inside a glass vessel, the blessing is not recited until one can see the actual body of the flame without interruption. Therefore, even if the candle is exposed and gives much light, if people are standing beside it blocking the view of the flame, one does not recite the blessing. Even when one can see the flame, he must come close enough to its light to be able to distinguish, by its light, between a coin of one country and a coin of another country of the same size. A blind person does not recite the blessing, since he does not benefit from the light. It is written in the book Torah LiShmah that although by strict law it suffices to be able to distinguish between coins, it is the most preferable fulfillment of the commandment to come even closer to the candle, so that its light reaches him in abundance.
takeaways: The blessing is not recited until one sees the actual body of the flame without interruption
Even when the flame is visible, one should come close enough to distinguish, by its light, between similar coins
A blind person does not recite the blessing
It is the most preferable fulfillment of the commandment to come even closer to the candle

paragraphs: Kesheyyebarek al hanner, yakop rashe etzbeotayv haymanim el tok kappo, veyihyeh haggudal mekusseh tachat haarba etzbaot, veyihyu nikpapim lipne hanner velipne haadam atzmo. velo yaaseh keotam hannohagim lehistakkel beachare haetzbaot bihyotam peshutim, bilti kepupim; vegam lo yaaseh keotam hannohagim lasim pene haetzbaot zequpot keneged hanner, veaach"k kopepim otam, velo keotam shemmehappekim pene hakkap kelappe haqqarqa, vaachore haetzbaot shehu meqom hatztzippareniyyim kelappe mala lashshamayim, vekannizkar kol zeh bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l. veap al pi demuttar lebarek al ner shumman o shel cheleb, mikkol maqom, al pi hassod tob lebarek al ner shel shaava; gam yoter nakon lebarek al abuqa, dehaynu shette nerot shaava qeluim yachad, vekannizkar beminhage rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot. umi shehibdil kebar leatzmo vechozer umabdil laacherim, "p sheyyukal lebarek lahem birkat hahabdala, lo yebarek lahem birkat "meore haesh", deyesh pelugta bazeh vesapeq berakot lehaqel, ella yebareku hem.

clarification.explanation: When reciting the blessing over the candle, one should curl the fingertips of the right hand into the palm, with the thumb covered beneath the four fingers, which are curled facing the candle and the person's face. One should not follow the practice of those who look at the backs of the fingers while they are outstretched, nor of those who hold the fingers upright facing the candle and only then curl them, nor of those who turn the palm toward the ground with the nails facing upward, as is explained in the words of the Ari. Although it is permitted to bless over a candle of tallow or fat, according to the esoteric tradition it is good to bless over a wax candle, and it is even more proper to bless over a torch, that is, two wax candles braided together. One who has already performed Havdalah for himself and then performs it again for others — even though he may recite for them the blessing of Havdalah, he should not recite for them "Who creates the lights of fire," since there is a dispute about this and we are lenient in a doubt concerning blessings; rather, they should recite it themselves.
takeaways: The fingertips of the right hand are curled into the palm, with the thumb covered, facing the candle and one's face
According to the esoteric tradition it is good to bless over a wax candle, and even better over a torch of two braided wax candles
One who performs Havdalah again for others should not recite "Who creates the lights of fire" for them; they should recite it themselves

paragraphs: Kol otam shehashlicha tzibbur motziam yede chobatam, yittenu enehem bakkos bishat habberaka, velo yazuzu mimmeqomam ad sheyyigmor hashlicha tzibbur birkat hammabdil kullah; velo keotam habburim asher darkam lehishshamet aneh vaana, deponim laleket velatzet: zeh poneh lilbosh minalayv, vezeh poneh lechappes achar beno o achar chabero laleket immo, venimtza mesirim datam meiqqar birkat hahabdala, deen shomeim otah kullah.

clarification.explanation: All those whom the prayer leader exempts through Havdalah should fix their eyes on the cup during the blessing, and should not move from their place until the prayer leader has finished the entire blessing of "HaMavdil." They should not act like the ignorant, whose way is to slip away here and there and leave: one turns to put on his shoes, another looks for his son or friend to leave with, and they end up distracted from the essence of the blessing of Havdalah and do not hear all of it, and do not fulfill their obligation.
takeaways: Those hearing Havdalah from the prayer leader should fix their eyes on the cup and not move until the blessing is finished
One should not slip away in the middle, lest he become distracted and not hear the whole blessing

paragraphs: Mi sheazenayv kebedot veeno yakol lishmoa birkat "hammabdil" mishshelicha tzibbur, veen lo yayin lehabdil alayv - hare zeh mistakkel veroeh bekos hayyayin shebbeyad shelicha tzibbur, veomer birkat "hammabdil" kullah; v"p sheen ochez hakkos beyado - sheat haddechaq shane, dezeh hekreach gadol; vehammabdil yishteh hakkos, veen tzarik lehatim laacherim; veim eno yakol lishtoto, yitamennu meat, veyishtehu adam acher shekkivven alayv. venohagin lishpok meat yayin mehakkos al haaretz lesiman tob, vezeh yaaseh achar shetiyyato sheyyashiru bo dabar muat. veqodem sheyyishpok, yatbil rashe etzbeotayv beellu hashshiyyurin veyaabirem al mitzcho lechibbub metzuvveh.

clarification.explanation: One whose ears are heavy and cannot hear the blessing of "HaMavdil" from the prayer leader, and who has no wine to perform Havdalah himself, should look at the cup of wine in the prayer leader's hand and say the entire blessing of "HaMavdil" himself. Even though he is not holding the cup in his own hand, a time of pressing need is different, since this is a great necessity. The prayer leader performing Havdalah drinks the cup himself and need not give others a taste from it; if he cannot drink it, he should taste a little from it and let another person, who intended to fulfill his obligation through it, drink it. It is customary to pour a little wine from the cup onto the ground as a good sign, and this is done after drinking, when a little remains in the cup. Before pouring it out, one should dip his fingertips in the leftover wine and pass them over his forehead, out of affection for the commandment.
takeaways: One with impaired hearing and no wine looks at the cup in the prayer leader's hand and says the whole blessing himself
A time of pressing need permits this even without holding the cup
It is customary to pour a little wine on the ground as a good sign after drinking
One dips his fingertips in the leftover wine and passes them over his forehead, out of affection for the commandment

paragraphs: Kevan shehiggia sapeq chasheka, asur leekol o lishtot ad sheyyabdil. veim haya yosheb veokel mibbeod yom vechasheka lo, en tzarik lehapsiq, umuttar sheyyigmor kirtzono. veim hipsiq vehitpallel arbit, apillu im adayin lo chasheka - asur leekol velishtot ad sheyyabdil, kevan shehitpallel arbit; veha deamerinan behaya yosheb veokel deqaba atzmo laakila, deeno tzarik lehapsiq, haynu davqa im hitchil qodem chatzi shaa lachasheka, abal im hitchil tok chatzi shaa, az asur leekol kesheyyaggia sapeq chasheka ad sheyyabdil. veyesh lehizzaher shello lehabdil beemtza hasseuda o beemtza hashshetiyya, mishshum deyesh pelugta im yebarek "bore peri haggapen" al kos hahabdala o lo, veken yesh pelugta im tzarik lachazor ulebarek al haakila sheyyokal aach"k kesheyyigmor seuddato.

clarification.explanation: Once "doubtful darkness" (the twilight at the conclusion of the Sabbath) has arrived, it is forbidden to eat or drink until one performs Havdalah. But if one was sitting and eating while it was still day and darkness fell on him, he need not stop, and may finish as he wishes. If he paused and prayed the evening prayer, even if it is not yet dark, it is forbidden to eat and drink until he performs Havdalah, since he has prayed the evening prayer. The permission for one sitting and eating (not needing to stop) applies specifically if he began more than half an hour before dark; but if he began within the half hour, it is forbidden to eat from the arrival of doubtful darkness until he performs Havdalah. One should be careful not to perform Havdalah in the middle of a meal or of drinking, since there is a dispute as to whether one should recite "Who creates the fruit of the vine" over the cup of Havdalah, and likewise whether one must recite a new blessing over what he eats afterward when he finishes.
takeaways: Doubtful darkness at the conclusion of the Sabbath — eating and drinking are forbidden until Havdalah; but one already sitting and eating from before need not stop (if he began more than half an hour before dark)

Having prayed the evening prayer — forbidden until Havdalah, even if not yet dark; and Havdalah should not be performed in the middle of a meal or drinking (a dispute about the blessing over wine and repeating blessings on the food)

paragraphs: Im lo haya yosheb veokel ella raq haya yosheb veshoteh, deqaba atzmo lishtiyya bilbad - kesheyyaggia zeman shehu sapeq chasheka tzarik lehapsiq veasur lishtot od. veyesh bene-adam sheosim seuda shelishit vegomerim bebetam, ubaim letayyel bebet acherim beodam betok seuddatam, veyoshebim immahem bimsibba lishtot davqa, veen okelim immahem, ditzrikin ellu lizzaher, kevan shehiggia sapeq chasheka shello yishtu od. veda, dela neesra hashshetiyya middina, ella raq beyayin veshekar ushear mashqin, abal mayim, muttar; mihu yesh machmirin bemayim, mittaam acher.

clarification.explanation: If one was not sitting and eating but only sitting and drinking, having set himself specifically for drinking, when the time of doubtful darkness arrives he must stop and is forbidden to drink further. There are people who hold a third meal and finish it at home, and afterward go to visit others while still full, sitting with them only to drink without eating; these people must be careful that once doubtful darkness has arrived, they drink no more. Know that by strict law the prohibition on drinking applies only to wine, beer, and other beverages, but water is permitted; nevertheless some are stringent about water too, for another reason.
takeaways: One who set himself only for drinking must stop at doubtful darkness
One visiting others to drink after his own meal should be careful about this
The prohibition applies to wine, beer, and other beverages; water is permitted, though some are stringent about it too

paragraphs: Im nimsheka seuddato ad achar chasheka, vegamar seuddato verotzeh lebarek birkat hammazon: im darko tamid lebarek birkat hammazon al hakkos, yebarek gam atta al hakkos; abal besapeq chasheka, apillu en darko tamid bebirkat hammazon al hakkos, yebarek atta al hakkos. veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal ch', ot k', ushear acharonim. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti, dezeh ayre bedarko tamid lebarek al hakkos bisuda shelishit, abal mi sheddarko lebarek al hakkos bisuda rishona usheniyya, abal bisuda shelishit en darko lebarek al hakkos, eno mebarek atta. veken mi sheddarko lebarek tamid al hakkos bisuda shelishit, "p sheen darko lebarek tamid bisuda rishona usheniyya, hare zeh mebarek atta. vekatabti od, daapillu mi sheeno nizhar tamid - im rotzeh lebarek, en goarin bo, deyesh lo al mah lismok; veayyen "eliyya rabba" v"tosepet-shabbat" ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: If one's meal extended past dark and he finished it, and wants to recite Grace After Meals: if his usual practice is always to recite Grace After Meals over a cup, he should do so now as well. And even in a time of doubtful darkness, even if his usual practice is not always to recite it over a cup, he should recite it over a cup now. The Ben Ish Chai explains in his book Makbetzal that the matter depends specifically on one's custom at the third meal: one whose practice is to recite the blessing over a cup at the first and second meals but not at the third does not recite it over a cup now. One whose practice is to recite it over a cup at the third meal does recite it now, even if this is not his practice at the first and second. Even one who is not always careful about this — if he wants to recite it over a cup, he is not to be rebuked, since he has grounds to rely on.
takeaways: The meal extended past dark — one accustomed to reciting Grace over a cup should do so now
In doubtful darkness, even one not always accustomed does so now
The matter is measured specifically by one's custom at the third meal
One who wishes to recite it over a cup is not to be rebuked, since he has grounds to rely on

paragraphs: Ap al gab demiddina muttar lebarek meyushshab; veadderabba, mera"n beshulchan aruk katab shetztzarik lehabdil meyushshab, mishshum dekevan dehaechad poter et chabero, yesh lahem laasot qebiut, umeomed la have qebiut. vmvr"m za"l behaggahat hashshulchan hu dekatab demabdilin meummad, mikkol maqom matzinu sheyyesh meqomot shehem qibbelu horaat mera"n za"l, veim kol zeh nahagu lehabdil meummad, sheomedim hashlicha tzibbur vekol haqqahal kullam likbod hammelek, hu hashshabbat haqqadosh shemmelavvim oto, vederek leviyya – meummad; veken nohagim beirenu bagdad y" laamod kol haqqahal bishat hahabdala. veayyen "kap-hachayyim", si' l", avvat l"h. veshamati shebbeare haqqodesh tvb"b en maqpidin, umabdilin kepi mah sheyyizdammen - ben omedin, ben yoshebin - sheen medaqdeqin bazeh.

clarification.explanation: Although by strict law it is permitted to perform Havdalah seated, and indeed Maran in the Shulchan Aruch wrote that one must perform Havdalah seated — since one is exempting his fellow from the obligation, they should establish a fixed setting, and standing lacks such fixedness — the Rema wrote that Havdalah is performed standing. Nevertheless we find places that accepted Maran's ruling and yet were accustomed to perform Havdalah standing, since the prayer leader and the whole congregation stand in honor of the King, that is, the holy Sabbath, whom they accompany on its departure, and the manner of accompanying is standing. This is also the custom in Baghdad, where the whole congregation stands during Havdalah. The Ben Ish Chai heard that in the holy cities they are not particular about this, and perform Havdalah however it happens, whether standing or seated.
takeaways: Maran wrote that Havdalah is performed seated, for fixedness; the Rema wrote it is performed standing
In Baghdad the whole congregation stands, accompanying the King, the Sabbath, on its departure
In the holy cities they are not particular, and perform Havdalah however it happens

paragraphs: "g deikka pelugta beinyan hahabdala bedin hannashim - qayma lan lahalaka dehannashim yekolim lehabdil leatzman; velo od, ella gam mi shehibdil bebet-hakkeneset veyatza yede chobato, yakol lehabdil lahem, vekaasher heela ken lahalaka haggaon chida" za"l, veken nohagim poh irenu bagdad; mihu nireh li, deim haishsha yodaat lebarek, tob shettebarek vetabdil leatzmah, deen hannashim bene-samka lishmoa habberaka mittechilla vead sop mippi hammabdil.

clarification.explanation: Although there is a dispute regarding the law of women performing Havdalah, the halachah follows the opinion that women may perform Havdalah for themselves. Moreover, even one who has already performed Havdalah in the synagogue and fulfilled his own obligation may go back and perform it again for them to exempt them, as the Chida raised, and so is the custom in Baghdad. Nevertheless, it seems to the Ben Ish Chai that if the woman knows how to recite the blessing, it is good that she recite the blessing and perform Havdalah for herself, since women are not expert at hearing the entire blessing from beginning to end from the one performing Havdalah.
takeaways: Women may perform Havdalah for themselves
One who has already performed Havdalah may go back and perform it again to exempt women
If the woman knows how to recite the blessing, it is good that she perform Havdalah herself

paragraphs: Neenas velo hibdil belel motzae-shabbat, yesh lo zeman lehabdil ad sop yom shelishi; velo yebarek ella "bore peri haggapen" al hayyayin ubirkat "hammabdil"; mihu, birkat hammabdil yomar beli shem umalkut, mishshum deikka pelugta bazeh; velaken, kevan sheabera lel motzae-shabbat velo hibdil al hakkos, yomar birkat "hammabdil" beli shem umalkut, veraq yeharher shem umalkut belibbo. vehabdala deyom tob, en lah tashlumin, dekol sheabera hallayla shel motzae yom tob, en lo od zeman lehabdil.

clarification.explanation: One who was prevented by circumstances and did not perform Havdalah on the night of the Sabbath's conclusion has time to make it up and perform Havdalah until the end of Tuesday. He should recite only "Who creates the fruit of the vine" over the wine and the blessing of "HaMavdil," without the blessings over the spices and the candle. But he should say the blessing of "HaMavdil" without God's name and sovereignty, since there is a dispute about this, and should only have the name and sovereignty in mind in his heart. But the Havdalah of a festival has no make-up; once the night at the conclusion of the festival has passed, there is no longer any time to perform Havdalah.
takeaways: One who was prevented may make up Havdalah until the end of Tuesday
In the make-up, only "Who creates the fruit of the vine" and "HaMavdil" are recited, without the spices and candle
The blessing of "HaMavdil" in the make-up is said without God's name and sovereignty, held in mind instead
There is no make-up for the Havdalah of a festival

paragraphs: Asur laasot melaka qodem sheyyabdil. vehashshammash shetztzarik lehadliq ner lehabdala, kevan sheamar "atta chonantanu" bitpilla, muttar lehadliq hanner; mihu yesh omerim: "p sheamar "atta chonantanu", im kol zeh, qodem sheyyadliq hanner yomar birkat "hammabdil" beli shem umalkut, veken rauy lehorot, veken yaaseh apillu im lo hitpallel adayin, o im shakach lomar "atta chonantanu", sheyyomar birkat ha"mabdil" beli shem umalkut, veyadliq hanner. vehaadam yitten dato al mesharete habbayit lehazhiram bekak. veen madliqin hanner bemotza"sh ella ad achar qaddish titqabbel.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to do work at the conclusion of the Sabbath before performing Havdalah. The attendant who needs to light a candle for the purpose of Havdalah — since he has already said "Atah chonantanu" in the prayer, he is permitted to light the candle. Nevertheless, some say that even though he said "Atah chonantanu," before lighting the candle he should say "Blessed is He who distinguishes between the holy and the profane," without God's name and sovereignty, and it is proper to rule this way. He should do the same even if he has not yet prayed, or if he forgot to say "Atah chonantanu" — saying "Blessed is He who distinguishes" without God's name and sovereignty before lighting. A person must pay attention to the household servants to caution them about this. A candle is not lit at the conclusion of the Sabbath until after the Kaddish "Titkabel."
takeaways: It is forbidden to do work before Havdalah; one who said "Atah chonantanu" is permitted to light a candle
It is proper that before lighting the candle he say "Blessed is He who distinguishes between the holy and the profane," without God's name and sovereignty
The same applies to one who has not yet prayed or forgot "Atah chonantanu"
A candle is not lit at the conclusion of the Sabbath until after the Kaddish "Titkabel"

paragraphs: Meqomot hahanaa shennitqenu alehem arbaa berakot behabdala, matchil hasseder shellahem millematta lemala, vehu lesimana taba laasot hasseder derek aliyya, lirmoz degam haadam baasaqayv yihyeh hilluk vegadol. venohagim lomar pesuqim shel "veyitten leka veku'", kol echad beboo lebeto; ak rabbenu haari"y za"l, haya minhago leameram beet hahabdala al hakkos. venahagu gam ken lomar kol echad bebeto q"l (130) peamim "eliyyahu hannabi zakur lattob", sheoleh mispar arba tebot ellu arba meot, lehaknia arba meot kochot shel sitra-achra besod hakkatub (bereshit lg, ): "vehinneh esav ba vearba meot ish immo". ubeseper "tora lishmah" katub kavvana baamirat "eliyyahu hannabi zakur lattob" kemo shekkatabti - ki "eliyyahu" im ot Adonai shel "hannabi" hem otiyyot "el hvy"h" kesidran, veotiyyot "nabi" - mispar s"g keminyan shem s"g shemmimmennu happarnasa; veshemot "el hvy"h" - mispar "okel", shemmizzeh nimshak hammazon; veotiyyot "zakur" - mispar "hvy"h" deyodin v"ehyeh" deyodin; veotiyyot "lattob" - mispar chibbur "hvy"h" v"ehyeh"; yeuyyan sham. uminhago shel t"r adoni abi zlh"h lomar petichat eliyyahu zakur lattob qodem sheyyomar q"l peamim hannizkarim; veken anachnu nohagim atta bebetenu, dabar beitto mah tob umah naim. vedarkenu likpol pasuq "vaamartem koh lechay veku'" shishsha peamim, keneged shishsha qetzavot, vehayyesod kalul min shishsha qetzavot, lehamshik mimmennu shepa shalom lesheshet yeme hachol.

clarification.explanation: The four blessings of Havdalah are arranged from the lowest to the highest, as a good sign, to allude that a person too should go on rising higher and higher in his affairs. It is customary to say the verses "Vayiten lecha" ("And may God give you..."), each person upon arriving home, whereas the Ari would say them at the time of Havdalah over the cup. It is customary for each person to say at home, one hundred and thirty times, "Eliyahu HaNavi zachur latov" ("Elijah the Prophet, remembered for good"), since the numerical value of these four words equals four hundred, in order to subdue the four hundred forces of the "other side," in the secret of "and behold, Esau is coming, and four hundred men with him." It is written in the book Torah LiShmah that there is a further intention in saying this according to the esoteric tradition: "Eliyahu" together with the letter heh of "HaNavi" form the letters "El Yahweh" in order; the letters of "navi" equal, in number, 63, the numerical value of the Name of 63 (Sag), from which sustenance is drawn; the Names "El Havayah" equal the value of "ochel" (food), from which nourishment is drawn; the letters of "zachor" equal, in number, the value of "Havayah" spelled with yuds and "Ehyeh" spelled with yuds; and the letters of "latov" equal the combined value of "Havayah" and "Ehyeh" — meaning that in saying these very words one draws down, in a hidden way, sustenance and food. The custom of the Ben Ish Chai's father was to say the "opening of Eliyahu zachur latov" even before saying the aforementioned one hundred and thirty times, and this is their custom at home. It is their way to repeat the verse "and you shall say, thus, to life" six times, corresponding to the six directions, to draw an abundance of peace for the six weekdays.
takeaways: The four blessings of Havdalah are arranged from lowest to highest, as a sign that a person should rise ever higher
"Vayiten lecha" is said upon arriving home; the Ari said it during Havdalah over the cup
"Eliyahu HaNavi zachur latov" is said one hundred and thirty times, to subdue the four hundred forces of the "other side"
According to the esoteric tradition, the words allude to God's Names and to the numerical value of "food," drawing down sustenance
The verse "and you shall say, thus, to life" is repeated six times, corresponding to the six directions, to draw peace for the weekdays

paragraphs: Leolam yesadder adam shulchano bemotzae-shabbat belechem mishneh, vaapillu sheeno yakol leekol ella raq kazzayit - lelavvot hashshabbat bitziato. ukebar katabnu leel, ki lehamshakat tosepet qedushshat shabbat lime hachol mibbechinat hasseudot, osin seuda rebiit bemotzae-shabbat, umekavvenim bah kede lehamshik or qedushshat shabbat lekol seudot yeme hachol vekannizkar leel, vekamporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l. veyesh mishtaddelim lehabi al hashshulchan leekol ezeh dabar chadash - min peri o min mirqachat, umine matoq shello akelu mimmennu beshalosh seudot oto hayyom, umaalatah gedola shemmatztzelet mechabot haqqeber, vehi niqret al shem david hammelek alayv hashshalom. laken omerim qodem netila: "atqinu seudeta demehemanuta, da hi seudeta dedavid malka meshicha"; veomerim piyyutim hashshayyakim ledavid h"h betok hasseuda, gam bishbil limmud veeseq tora mittok seuda zo; al ken minhagenu lomar petichat eliyyahu zakur lattob od happaam betok seuda zo; vegam ki hu hambasser tob al malkut mashicha ben david sheyyabo bb". ulekak anachnu omerim bebirkot hahaptara: "sammechenu Adonai elohenu beeliyyahu hannabi abdeka, ubemalkut bet david meshichaka". veamarti bs"d: eliyyahu, missipro b"n, vedavid hammelek alayv hashshalom, missipro y"d; tzerup shenehem hu tebat "nedib"; vezeh sheamar bemishle, y"t, pasuq v: "rabbim yechallu pene nadib, vekol harea leish mattan"; perush: hakkol metzappim umeyachalim lirot pene nedib, hem david veeliyyahu, shehem y"d n"b, ak dabar zeh taluy beachdut ubitzdaqa; zehu "kol hara" shehu achdut, sheyyihyu yisrael raim zeh im zeh, veod taluy b"ish mattan" kemo shekkatub sham: "mattan basseter" shehu mattan hatztzedaqa; velazeh amar (shir hashshirim v.yb): "markebot ammi nedib", kelomar, "markebot ammi", hi teluya b"nedib", shehem david hammelek alayv hashshalom veeliyyahu zakur lattob.

clarification.explanation: A person should always set his table at the conclusion of the Sabbath with double bread, even if he can eat only an olive's-worth, in order to accompany the Sabbath on its departure. This is the fourth meal, meant, according to the esoteric tradition, to draw the additional holiness of the Sabbath, from the aspect of the meals, into all the weekday meals. Some make an effort to bring to the table something new — a fruit, a preserve, or sweets not eaten during the three Sabbath meals — and the virtue of this is great, saving one from the beating of the grave. This meal is named for King David, and therefore, before washing the hands, one says, "Atkinu se'udata dimheimenuta, da hi se'udata deDavid malka Meshicha" ("Prepare the meal of faith; this is the meal of David the Messiah King"), and poems related to David and Torah matters are said during it, since Elijah is the herald of the kingdom of the House of David, which will come speedily — and therefore in the blessings of the haftarah it is said, "Gladden us, O Lord our God, with Elijah the Prophet Your servant, and with the kingdom of the House of David Your anointed one." The Ben Ish Chai adds a numerical allusion: "Eliyahu" has the numerical value of "ben" (52), and King "David" has the value of "yud-dalet" (14), and their combination equals the spelling of "nadiv" (a generous or noble person); and this is what is said in Proverbs (19:6), "Many will entreat the favor of the noble (nadiv), and every man is a friend to one who gives gifts" — meaning that everyone longs to see the face of David and Elijah, but this depends on the unity of Israel with one another ("every man") and on giving charity in secret ("a friend to one who gives gifts"). This is why it is said in Song of Songs, "the chariots of my noble people" (nadiv), since the redemption of my people depends on the "nadiv" — King David and Elijah the Prophet.
takeaways: The table is set at the conclusion of the Sabbath with double bread, even for just an olive's-worth, to accompany the departing Sabbath
This is the fourth meal, drawing the Sabbath's holiness into the weekdays
It is good to bring something new to the table; its virtue saves from the beating of the grave
The meal is named for King David, and poems about David and Elijah are said
A numerical allusion: Eliyahu and David together equal "nadiv" (noble one), and redemption depends on unity and secret charity

paragraphs: Katab b"machaziq beraka" beshem seper hakkavvanot yashan, deen rauy lehitasseq bimlaka sheenah okel-nepesh o battora, ella ad achar sheyyaaseh seuda rebiit demotzae-shabbat. vekatebu haacharonim za"l, shello yasir bigde shabbat mealayv ella ad achar seuda rebiit; uzemannah, ad achar arba shaot. veyomar bebirkat hammazon "migdol" beva"v; veayyen "kap-hachayyim", ot n"t, yeuyyan sham. venireh li: "p shennatenu lah shiur ad achar arba shaot, haynu limtzuvva min hammubchar, abal im neenas, yukal leqayyemah ad chatzot layla, deha katab rabbenu za"l beshaar-hakkavvanot dead chatzi hallayla enah holakat qedushshat hashshabbat, velaken hizhir shello lomar vidduy bemotzae-shabbat qodem chatzot layla.

Vekol mi sheeno meqayyem seuda rebiit, nechshab lo keillu lo qiyyem seuda shelishit likbod shabbat, deaz nechshab lo sheakalah bishbil seudat hallayla, dekol adam darko kol layla leekol, veen zeh likbod shabbat; velaken ellu shemmitannim hapsaqot, asur lahem laasot hapsaqa bemotza"sh, deasur lehitannot belel motzae-shabbat; veayyen "kap-hachayyim" mah shekkatab bazeh. veim yihyeh haadam anus mechamat choli, veeno yakol leqayyem seuda rebiit, im kol zeh yesadder shulchano bimzonot uperot veyoklu bene beto, vehu gam ken yitam immahem min hashshulchan kepi yekaletto. katebu hamqubbalim: yesh etzem beadam sheeno neheneh mishshum akila, ella raq min seuda rebiit demotza"sh. veetzem zeh nishar qayyam baqqeber veen sholet bo riqqabon; veha niqra "niskoy", vegam niqra "luz", vegam niqra "betuel". veamarti bazeh remez - ki shelosha shemot shel etzem hannizkar hem rashe tebot "laban", vehem sope tebot sheloshet shemot shehem: yisrael yaaqob yeshurun; umizzeh haetzem yibneh haggup bitchiyyat hammetim; vezeh yihyeh leyisrael davqa, hanneemar bahem (debarim d,d): "veattem haddebeqim baAdonai elohekem, chayyim kullekem hayyom".

clarification.explanation: It is written in Machazik Berachah, in the name of an old book of Kavanot, that it is not proper to occupy oneself with work that is not for the sake of food, nor with Torah study, until after the fourth meal of the conclusion of the Sabbath has been held. The later authorities wrote that one should not remove his Sabbath clothes until after the fourth meal, whose time extends until four hours into the night. It seems to the Ben Ish Chai that the measure of four hours is for the most preferable fulfillment of the commandment, but one who was prevented by circumstances may fulfill it until midnight, since until midnight the holiness of the Sabbath does not depart. Anyone who does not hold the fourth meal is considered as though he had not held the third meal in honor of the Sabbath. Therefore those who observe fasts of atonement (ta'anit hafsakah) are forbidden to hold their "hafsakah" (final pre-fast meal) at the conclusion of the Sabbath, since it is forbidden to fast on the night of the Sabbath's conclusion. If one was prevented by illness and cannot hold the fourth meal, he should nevertheless set his table with grain foods and fruits for his household to eat, and he should taste a little with them as he is able. The kabbalists wrote that there is a bone in a person that derives no benefit from any eating except from the fourth meal at the conclusion of the Sabbath, and this bone remains intact in the grave, unaffected by decay, and from it the body will be rebuilt at the resurrection of the dead; this bone has three names: "Luz," "Betuel," and "Niskoi." The Ben Ish Chai alludes that these three names form the initials "Lavan," which are also the final letters of the three names "Yisrael, Ya'akov, Yeshurun" — and it is specifically in Israel that the verse is fulfilled, "And you who cling to the Lord your God are all alive today."
takeaways: One should not occupy himself with non-essential work or Torah study until after the fourth meal
One should not remove Sabbath clothes until after it; its time extends to four hours into the night, or until midnight if prevented by circumstances
One who does not hold the fourth meal is considered as though he did not hold the third meal in honor of the Sabbath
Those observing a fast of atonement may not hold their final pre-fast meal at the conclusion of the Sabbath

According to the kabbalists, a particular bone benefits only from this meal and remains intact for the resurrection; its three names form the initials "Lavan," the final letters of "Yisrael, Ya'akov, Yeshurun"
